'''James Calvin Young''' (born August 16, 1995) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Ipswich Force]] of the [[NBL1 North]]. He played one season of [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]] before being selected with the 17th overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]] by the [[Boston Celtics]]. He spent the majority of his rookie NBA season playing in the NBA Development League for the Celtics' affiliate team, the [[Maine Red Claws]]. In 2019–20 he was the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League Statistical Leaders|top scorer in the Israel Basketball Premier League]], with an average of 20.5 points per game.

==High school career==
[[File:20130403 MCDAAG James Young slashing layup (3).JPG|thumb|left|upright|Young slashes for a layup in the [[2013 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]]]]
Young attended both [[Troy High School (Michigan)|Troy High School]] in [[Troy, Michigan]], and [[Rochester High School (Michigan)|Rochester High School]] in [[Rochester Hills, Michigan]]. As a junior at Troy in 2011–12, Young averaged 25.1 points, 10.5 rebounds, 4.5 assists and 2.5 steals per game, earning first-team All-State honors from the Associated Press, Detroit News and Detroit Free Press.<ref name=bio>{{cite web|url=http://www.ukathletics.com/sport/m-baskbl/2015/roster/559d90b4e4b01c7eefd5ee7f|title=Bio for James Young|work=UKAthletics.com|access-date=April 18, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170427154536/http://www.ukathletics.com/sport/m-baskbl/2015/roster/559d90b4e4b01c7eefd5ee7f|archive-date=April 27, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On October 11, 2012, Young signed a [[National Letter of Intent|letter of intent]] to play college basketball for the [[University of Kentucky]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/story/2012-10-11/james-young-kentucky-basketball-recruiting-john-calipari|title=Kentucky lands James Young, its third top-10 recruit|work=SportingNews.com|date=October 12, 2012|access-date=January 6, 2013|archive-date=November 12, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131112120040/http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/story/2012-10-11/james-young-kentucky-basketball-recruiting-john-calipari|url-status=dead}}</ref> As a senior at Rochester in 2012–13, Young averaged 27.2 points, 16.0 rebounds and 5.7 assists per game, going on to earn McDonald's All-American honors losing twice to Rochester Adams High School.<ref name="bio" />

Considered a five-star recruit by [[ESPN.com]], Young was listed as the No. 3 small forward and the No. 8 player in the nation in 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/104892/james-young|title=James Young Recruiting Profile|work=ESPN.com|access-date=April 18, 2014}}</ref>

==College career==
As a freshman at [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] in 2013–14, Young finished second in UK single-season freshman history with 82 made three-pointers on the season. He was named [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] Freshman of the Week two times, earned second-team All-SEC honors, SEC All-Freshman team honors, and was named to the Final Four NCAA All-Tournament team.<ref name="bio" /> In 40 games (39 starts), he averaged 14.3 points, 4.3 rebounds and 1.7 assists in 32.4 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/james-young-1.html |title=James Young Stats |work=Sports-Reference.com |access-date=April 18, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140410143236/http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/james-young-1.html |archive-date=April 10, 2014 }}</ref> Early in the season, on November 19, he scored a career-high 26 points and hit five three-pointers in a 105–76 win over [[Texas–Arlington Mavericks men's basketball|UT Arlington]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400502345|title=James Young leads No. 4 Kentucky to rout of UT Arlington|work=ESPN.com|date=November 19, 2013|access-date=November 11, 2015}}</ref>

On April 17, 2014, Young declared for the [[NBA draft]], forgoing his final three years of college eligibility.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2014/story/_/id/10797286/james-young-kentucky-wildcats-declares-nba-draft|title=James Young declares for draft|work=ESPN.com|date=April 18, 2014|access-date=April 18, 2014}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Boston Celtics (2014–2017)===

====2014–15 season====
[[File:James Young Celtics.jpg|thumb|right|Young with the Celtics in 2014]]
On June 26, 2014, Young was selected with the 17th overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]] by the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/sidebar/celtics-fill-needs-drafting-smart-young|title=Celtics Fill Needs by Drafting Smart, Young|work=NBA.com|date=June 27, 2014|access-date=June 27, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/boston/nba/story/_/id/11141252/2014-nba-draft-boston-celtics-take-marcus-smart-no-6-pick|title=Celtics draft guard Marcus Smart|work=ESPN.com|date=June 27, 2014|access-date=June 27, 2014}}</ref> On July 10, 2014, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Celtics.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-sign-2014-draft-picks | title=Celtics Sign 2014 Draft Picks | work=NBA.com | date=July 10, 2014 | access-date=July 10, 2014}}</ref> Injuries forced Young to miss the summer league, most of training camp and part of the early season. Because of these setbacks, Young spent much of the season driving back and forth between Boston and Maine, playing for the [[Maine Red Claws|Red Claws]] in order to receive consistent playing time.<ref>{{cite web | last=Hughes | first=Wally | url=http://hoopshabit.com/2015/01/07/boston-celtics-james-young-bostons-next-star/ | title=Boston Celtics: Is James Young Boston's Next Star? | work=HoopsHabit.com | date=January 7, 2015 | access-date=November 11, 2015}}</ref> He had 11 [[NBA Development League|D-League]] assignments in total during his rookie season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/all-time-nba-assignments/|title=All-Time NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=November 3, 2015}}</ref> Playing in the D-League was something Young was originally against, but grew to love in time, even urging the Celtics to send him to Maine during the month of December.<ref>{{cite web|last=Blakely |first=A. Sherrod |url=http://www.csnne.com/blog/celtics-talk/young-now-embracing-d-league-opportunities |title=Young now embracing D-League opportunities |work=CSNNE.com |date=December 29, 2014 |access-date=November 11, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151208110731/http://www.csnne.com/blog/celtics-talk/young-now-embracing-d-league-opportunities |archive-date=December 8, 2015 }}</ref> Young finally got an opportunity to shine for the Celtics on January 5, 2015, scoring a season-high 13 points in a loss to the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Robb | first=Brian | url=http://www.boston.com/sports/basketball/celtics/extras/celtics_blog/2015/01/james_young_shines_in_celtics_loss_to_hornets.html | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150107040555/http://www.boston.com/sports/basketball/celtics/extras/celtics_blog/2015/01/james_young_shines_in_celtics_loss_to_hornets.html | url-status=dead | archive-date=January 7, 2015 | title=James Young Shines in Celtics' Loss to Hornets | work=Boston.com | date=January 5, 2015 | access-date=November 11, 2015}}</ref> In light of this performance, Young had a solid run of playing time in [[Brad Stevens]]' rotation, averaging 3.8 points in 12.9 minutes per game between January 5 and March 6.<ref name=br>{{cite web | url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/y/youngja01/gamelog/2015/ | title=James Young 2014–15 Game Log | work=Basketball-Reference.com | access-date=November 11, 2015}}</ref> However, following that string of opportunities, Young managed just four more appearances to close out the regular season, and failed to appear in any of the Celtics' four playoff games against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref name="br" />

In 19 games for the Red Claws in 2014–15, Young averaged 20.7 points, 5.2 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.4 steals per game.<ref name=d-league>{{cite web | url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/dleague/players/y/youngja01d.html | title=James Young D-League Stats | work=Basketball-Reference.com | access-date=November 11, 2015}}</ref>

====2015–16 season====
In July 2015, Young joined the Celtics for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]], where he averaged 9.4 points and 3.4 rebounds in five games. His performance was considered underwhelming, as he shot just 27.1% from the field and 22.7% from three-point range.<ref name=sand>{{cite web | last=Sandgrund | first=Max | url=http://www.celticslife.com/2015/10/is-james-young-ready-to-help-fix.html | title=Is James Young ready to help fix the Celtics greatest weakness? | work=CelticsLife.com | date=October 27, 2015 | access-date=November 11, 2015}}</ref> He subsequently played the fewest preseason minutes of anyone who made the final 2015–16 opening night roster.<ref name="sand" /> Despite this, on October 30, the Celtics exercised their third-year team option on Young's rookie scale contract, extending the contract through the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/Celtics-Exercise-Options-on%20Smart-Young-Olynyk | title=Celtics Exercise Options on Smart, Young & Olynyk | work=NBA.com | date=October 30, 2015 | access-date=November 11, 2015}}</ref> His early 2015–16 season opportunities mirrored his rookie season, as he spent five days with the Red Claws between November 3 and 9 on two different assignments<ref name=assign>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/assignments/ |title=2015–16 NBA Assignments |work=NBA.com |access-date=November 11, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150906020056/http://dleague.nba.com/news/assignments/ |archive-date=September 6, 2015 }}</ref> before finally making his season debut for the Celtics on November 10, playing in the final 49 seconds of the team's 99–83 win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151110/BOSMIL/gameinfo.html|title=Thomas leads Celtics to 99–83 win over Bucks|work=NBA.com|date=November 10, 2015|access-date=November 11, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151114020929/http://www.nba.com/games/20151110/BOSMIL/gameinfo.html|archive-date=November 14, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> He received three more assignments to Maine following this.<ref name="assign" /> After playing in three games for the Celtics between November 24 and December 3, he almost got on a plane from San Antonio to Maine on December 4, but was informed not to minutes before boarding; the Celtics needed Young as insurance because of a quad injury to [[Avery Bradley]]. Young ultimately did not play for the Celtics against the [[San Antonio Spurs|Spurs]] on December 5.<ref>{{cite web|last=Blakely|first=A. Sherrod|url=http://www.csnne.com/boston-celtics/james-young-man-move-celtics|title=James Young is a man on the move for Celtics|work=CSNNE.com|date=December 5, 2015|access-date=December 6, 2015}}</ref> He went on to appear in seven of the team's next eight games, averaging 14.3 minutes per game over that stretch.<ref name=log>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/y/youngja01/gamelog/2016/|title=James Young 2015–16 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|date=December 30, 2015}}</ref> Young received seven more assignments to the Red Claws in 2016<ref name="assign" /> and appeared in three of the Celtics' six playoff games against the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref name="log" />

In 16 games for the Red Claws in 2015–16, Young averaged 14.8 points, 5.6 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 1.0 steals per game.<ref name="d-league" />

====2016–17 season====
In July 2016, Young re-joined the Celtics for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]], where he averaged 7.5 points and 2.8 rebounds in six games. On October 24, 2016, Young was retained by the Celtics for the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite web|last=Snow|first=Taylor C.|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/sidebar/prac-102416-james-young-earns-celtics-final-roster-spot|title=James Young Earns Celtics' Final Roster Spot|work=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2016|access-date=October 24, 2016}}</ref> On November 12, 2016, in the Celtics' ninth game of the season, Young scored a season-high 12 points in a 105–99 win over the [[Indiana Pacers]]. Young went unassigned in 2016–17 but only managed 29 games during the regular season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/y/youngja01/gamelog/2017/|title=James Young 2016–17 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=May 5, 2017}}</ref>

===2017 off-season===
In July 2017, Young became a [[free agent]] and joined the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] for the [[2017 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Kushner|first=Scott|url=http://www.theadvocate.com/new_orleans/sports/pelicans/article_401665c2-6371-11e7-b4f8-db233f0b1408.html|title=Remember James Young? The former Celtics first-round pick is looking for a niche with the Pelicans|work=TheAdvocate.com|date=July 7, 2017|access-date=July 10, 2017}}</ref> On September 6, 2017, he signed a training camp contract with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-sign-james-young|title=BUCKS SIGN JAMES YOUNG|work=NBA.com|date=September 6, 2017|access-date=September 6, 2017}}</ref> He was waived by the Bucks on October 5, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=20870|title=Bucks waive James Young|work=InsideHoops.com|date=October 5, 2017|access-date=October 5, 2017}}</ref>

===Wisconsin Herd (2017–2018)===
On October 22, 2017, Young was named in the inaugural [[Wisconsin Herd]] training camp roster.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://wisconsin.gleague.nba.com/news/wisconsin-herd-announce-training-camp-roster/|title=Wisconsin Herd Announce Training Camp Roster|work=NBA.com|date=October 22, 2017|access-date=October 22, 2017|archive-date=October 24, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171024102549/http://wisconsin.gleague.nba.com/news/wisconsin-herd-announce-training-camp-roster/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He went on to earn a spot in the team's opening-night roster.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/wisconsin-herd-finalizes-roster-inaugural-season|title=WISCONSIN HERD FINALIZES ROSTER FOR INAUGURAL SEASON|work=NBA.com|date=November 2, 2017|access-date=November 2, 2017}}</ref>

===Philadelphia 76ers (2018)===
On January 5, 2018, Young was signed to a [[two-way contract]] by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. Under the terms of the deal, Young split his playing time for the year between the 76ers and their G League affiliate, the [[Delaware Blue Coats|Delaware 87ers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/76ers-sign-james-young-two-way-contract|title=76ers Sign James Young to Two-Way Contract|work=NBA.com|date=January 5, 2018|access-date=January 5, 2018}}</ref> On March 26, 2018, Young was waived by the 76ers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/james-young-waived-by-sixers/|title=James Young: Waived by Sixers|work=cbssports.com|date=March 26, 2018|access-date=March 26, 2018}}</ref>

===Second stint with Wisconsin Herd (2018–2019)===
In October 2018, Young re-joined the [[Wisconsin Herd]].<ref name=gleague1819>{{cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/transactions/league/2019|title=2018–2019 G League Transactions|work=RealGM.com|access-date=November 4, 2018}}</ref> On January 18, 2019, he was waived by the Herd.<ref name="gleague1819" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://wisconsin.gleague.nba.com/news/herd-acquires-andre-spight/|title=Herd Acquires Andre Spight|work=NBA.com|date=January 18, 2019|access-date=January 18, 2019|archive-date=April 17, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190417185122/https://wisconsin.gleague.nba.com/news/herd-acquires-andre-spight/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Maccabi Haifa (2019–2020)===
On August 8, 2019, Young signed a one-year deal with [[Maccabi Haifa B.C.|Maccabi Haifa]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli Premier League]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/james-young-signs-with-maccabi-haifa/|title=James Young signs with Maccabi Haifa|date=August 8, 2019|publisher=Sportando|access-date=August 8, 2019|archive-date=March 18, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230318220644/https://sportando.basketball/en/james-young-signs-with-maccabi-haifa/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On November 14, 2019, Young recorded a career-high 32 points, shooting 9-of-17 from the field, along with five rebounds and three assists, leading Haifa to a 95–83 win over [[Hapoel Gilboa Galil]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://basket.co.il/game-zone.asp?GameId=24033&lang=en|title=Winner League, Game 2: M. Haifa Vs Gilboa Galil|date=November 14, 2019|publisher=basket.co.il|access-date=November 14, 2019}}</ref> On December 22, 2019, Young tied his career-high 32 points, while shooting 7-of-11 from three-point range, along with eight rebounds and three steals in a 92–60 blowout win over [[Hapoel Holon B.C.|Hapoel Holon]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://basket.co.il/game-zone.asp?GameId=24085&lang=en|title=Winner League, Game 11: M. Haifa Vs U-NET Holon|date=December 22, 2019|publisher=basket.co.il|access-date=December 22, 2019}}</ref> He averaged 20.3 points, 5.2 rebounds, 1.9 assists, and 1.4 steals per game for the team.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Varney |first1=Dennis |title=Catch up with 36 ex-Cats playing pro basketball in leagues outside the NBA |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/ex-cats/article241420196.html |access-date=May 16, 2020 |work=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]] |date=March 26, 2020}}</ref> In 2019–20 he was the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League Statistical Leaders|top scorer in the Israel Basketball Premier League]], with an average of 20.5 points per game.<ref name="auto">[🖉{{Cite web|url=http://basket.co.il/leaders.asp?cYear=2020&lang=en|title=ISRAEL BASKETBALL SUPER LEAGUE | 2019–20 Season | Regular Season | Statistics – Leaders|website=basket.co.il}}</ref>

===Westchester Knicks (2020–2021)===
On December 14, 2020, Young was signed by the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite tweet |user=NY_KnicksPR |number=1338649768877301760 |date=December 14, 2020 |title=The New York Knicks announced today that the team has signed guard James Young}}</ref> He was waived before the start of the season and assigned to the Knicks' G League affiliate, the [[Westchester Knicks]].

===Hapoel Tel Aviv (2021–2022)===
On March 8, 2021, he signed with [[Hapoel Tel Aviv B.C.|Hapoel Tel Aviv]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/james-young-joins-hapoel-tel-aviv/|title=James Young joins Hapoel Tel Aviv|last=|first=|date=March 8, 2021|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=March 8, 2021}}</ref>

===Kolossos Rodou (2023)===
On January 12, 2023, Young signed with Greek club [[Kolossos Rodou B.C.|Kolossos Rodou]] for the rest of the season. In 10 league games, he averaged 9.1 points and 3.3 rebounds, playing around 16 minutes per contest.

===Universo Treviso Basket (2023–2024)===
On July 22, 2023, he signed with [[Universo Treviso Basket|Treviso Basket]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/james-young-joins-nutribullet-treviso/|title=James Young joins Nutribullet Treviso|last=|first=|date=July 22, 2023|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=July 23, 2023}}</ref>

===Ipswich Force (2025)===
On April 14, 2025, Young was announced on the roster of the [[Ipswich Force]] for the 2025 [[NBL1 North]] season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ipswich Force NBL1 North men's player announcement |url=https://ipswichbasketball.com.au/latest-news-1/f/ipswich-force-nbl1-north-mens-player-announcement |website=Ipswich Basketball |access-date=April 27, 2025 |date=April 14, 2025}}</ref>
